   1: \subsection{Uniform score, stopping, plug-in, and two-point lemmas}
   2: \label{subsec:singular-uniform-lemmas-main}
   3: 
   4: \begin{lemma}[Uniform sampled-bin and sampled-tail derivatives]
   5: \label{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}
   6: For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
   7: physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
   8: \(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
   9: \(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
  10: multi-index \(a\),
  11: \[
  12: \begin{aligned}
  13:  \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
  14:  &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
  15:  \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
  16:  &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
  17: \end{aligned}
  18: \tag{U1}
  19: \]
  20: All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\).  In addition,
  21: \(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).
  22: \end{lemma}
  23: 
  24: \begin{proof}
  25: Compress the colliding holding times into \(Y=X_1+X_2\).  Relative to
  26: Lebesgue measure on \((0,\infty)^{n-1}\), the complete holding-time density is
  27: \[
  28:  f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)
  29:  =(c^2-\delta)e^{-cy}\frac{\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)}{\sqrt\delta}
  30:  \prod_{j=3}^n\theta_j e^{-\theta_jx_j},
  31: \tag{U2}
  32: \]
  33: where the quotient at \(\delta=0\) is \(y\).  Write
  34: \(\sinh(\sqrt\delta\,y)/\sqrt\delta=y h(\delta y^2)\), where
  35: \(h(x)=\sinh(\sqrt x)/\sqrt x\) is positive and analytic on
  36: \([0,\infty)\).  On a sufficiently small common neighbourhood,
  37: \(c^2-\delta\) and every rate are bounded away from zero.  The derivatives
  38: through order three of \(\log h(x)\) are bounded on \([0,\infty)\): they are
  39: continuous at zero by the power series, and their elementary hyperbolic
  40: expressions are bounded as \(x\to\infty\).  Differentiating \(\log f_q\)
  41: therefore gives, uniformly on \(\mathcal Q^+\),
  42: \[
  43:  |\partial_q^a\log f_q(y,x_3,\ldots,x_n)|
  44:  \le C_a\{1+(y+x_3+\cdots+x_n)^{2|a|}\},
  45:  \qquad 1\le |a|\le3.
  46: \tag{U3}
  47: \]
  48: 
  49: Put \(W=Y+X_3+\cdots+X_n\).  Differentiation under the integral in a
  50: sampling bin expresses every derivative of \(\log g_q(k)\) through order
  51: three as a finite universal polynomial in conditional expectations of the
  52: complete-data derivatives in \textup{(U3)}, conditional on
  53: \(k\Delta\tau<W\le(k+1)\Delta\tau\).  On this event every nonnegative
  54: holding time is at most \((k+1)\Delta\tau\), which proves the first bound in
  55: \textup{(U1)}.  This argument controls the ratio by the bin probability
  56: itself and hence does not infer a relative bound from an absolute derivative
  57: bound.
  58: 
  59: For the tail ratios, each exponential density is log-concave, convolution
  60: preserves log-concavity, and integration over a half-line shows that the
  61: survival function of \(W\) is log-concave.  Thus \(W\) is IFR and its residual
  62: life satisfies
  63: \[
  64:  \PP_q(W-t>x\mid W>t)\le \PP_q(W>x),\qquad t,x\ge0.
  65: \tag{U4}
  66: \]
  67: All rates on \(\mathcal Q^+\) exceed a common \(\underline\theta>0\), so
  68: \(W\) is stochastically dominated by an
  69: Erlang\((n,\underline\theta)\) variable.  Consequently, for every fixed
  70: integer \(m\),
  71: \[
  72:  \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}\EE_q(W^m\mid W>t)
  73:  \le C_m(1+t)^m.
  74: \tag{U5}
  75: \]
  76: The same conditional-score polynomial argument, now conditional on
  77: \(W>k\Delta\tau\), proves the second bound in \textup{(U1)}.  Finally,
  78: stochastic domination by the Erlang variable gives the common
  79: polynomial-exponential mass envelope.  The envelopes justify every
  80: differentiation under the integral and continuity at \(\delta=0\).
  81: \end{proof}
  82: 
  83: \begin{lemma}[Uniform stopped renewal-score CLT and LLN]
  84: \label{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}
  85: Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
  86: support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
  87: stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
  88: gaps, with initial age \(A_N\) and terminal residual \(R_N\), and put
  89: \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in \(q\in\mathcal Q\), and also for
  90: triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
  91: \[
  92:  K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),
  93: \qquad
  94:  \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
  95: \tag{U6}
  96: \]
  97: If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous,
  98: \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
  99: \[
 100:  \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
 101:  \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
 102:  \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
 103:  \right)\longrightarrow0.
 104: \tag{U7}
 105: \]
 106: For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
 107: \[
 108:  N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
 109:  -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
 110: \tag{U8}
 111: \]
 112: uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
 113: \(N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)\) uniformly.  These conclusions
 114: hold jointly and hence apply to the score, stopped Hessian, and third-order
 115: likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local triangular arrays.
 116: \end{lemma}
 117: 
 118: \begin{proof}
 119: The common exponential moment gives uniform bounds for every moment of
 120: \(D\), with \(0<\inf_q\mu_q\le\sup_q\mu_q<\infty\).  For the ordinary
 121: renewal count, compare the partial sums of \(D_j-\mu_q\) at
 122: \(\lfloor N/\mu_q\pm x\sqrt N\rfloor\).  Chebyshev's inequality and
 123: Kolmogorov's maximal inequality give a bound \(C/x^2\), uniformly in \(q\),
 124: for deviation of the count by more than \(x\sqrt N\).  The stationary delay
 125: changes this count only through the initial incomplete cycle, which is
 126: \(O_P(\log N)\) by the bound below.  This proves the first part of
 127: \textup{(U6)} without requiring independence between a reward and its cycle
 128: length.
 129: 
 130: The equilibrium formula
 131: \(\PP_q(A_N\ge t)=\mu_q^{-1}\sum_{j\ge t}S_q(j)\), and its terminal analogue,
 132: have a common exponential-polynomial bound.  There are at most \(N\) complete
 133: gaps because \(D\ge1\).  A union bound for those gaps and the two endpoint
 134: variables therefore makes the probability that the maximum exceeds
 135: \(C_0\log N\) tend to zero uniformly for sufficiently large \(C_0\).  This
 136: proves the second part of \textup{(U6)}.
 137: 
 138: For \(m_N=\lfloor N/\mu_q\rfloor\), the triangular-array Lindeberg theorem
 139: applied to the deterministic sum of \(b_q(G_j)\) gives the normal law in
 140: \textup{(U7)}.  The common polynomial envelope and exponential moment verify
 141: Lindeberg uniformly.  Replacing \(m_N\) by \(K_N\) changes the sum by at most
 142: the maximum of centred partial sums over \(O_P(\sqrt N)\) indices.
 143: Kolmogorov's inequality makes that difference \(o_P(\sqrt N)\) uniformly;
 144: this is the stopped-score, or Anscombe, step.  The same replacement in a
 145: law of large numbers is \(o_P(N)\), proving \textup{(U8)}.  The last assertion
 146: follows from \(K_N=O_P(N)\) and uniform integrability of the envelope.
 147: 
 148: To verify the displayed uniformity rather than only pointwise convergence,
 149: take an arbitrary parameter sequence.  Compactness supplies a convergent
 150: subsequence; parameter continuity plus the common exponential envelope gives
 151: convergence of the means, covariance matrices, Lindeberg terms, and all LLN
 152: integrals along it.  The preceding inequalities have constants independent of
 153: the subsequence.  Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence with
 154: the asserted joint limits, which is the uniform subsequence criterion and
 155: also proves the triangular-array statement.
 156: \end{proof}
 157: 
 158: \begin{lemma}[Efficient-score plug-in equicontinuity]
 159: \label{lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
 160: On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
 161: as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
 162: \[
 163:  \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
 164:  \qquad
 165:  \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
 166:  \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
 167: \tag{U9}
 168: \]
 169: For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
 170: \[
 171:  \sup_{\eta}\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
 172:  |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
 173:  =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
 174: \tag{U10}
 175: \]
 176: The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
 177: empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
 178: in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
 179: \(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
 180: the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
 181: \end{lemma}
 182: 
 183: \begin{proof}
 184: Uniform nondegeneracy makes the projection coefficient in \textup{(U9)} twice
 185: continuously differentiable with polynomial score envelopes.  By construction,
 186: \[
 187:  \EE_{\eta,0}\psi_\eta=0,
 188:  \qquad \EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
 189: \tag{U11}
 190: \]
 191: Differentiating the first identity, justified by
 192: \Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}, gives
 193: \[
 194:  \EE_{\eta,0}(\partial_\eta\psi_\eta)
 195:  =-\EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
 196: \tag{U12}
 197: \]
 198: Thus the derivative of \(\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}\) is a normalized stopped sum
 199: of centred rewards and is \(O_P(1)\) uniformly by
 200: \Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}.  A second-order Taylor expansion
 201: over a ball of radius \(L/\sqrt N\) has first term \(O_P(N^{-1/2})\); its
 202: second term is bounded by
 203: \(N^{-1/2}O_P(N)O(N^{-1})=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).  This proves \textup{(U10)}.
 204: The stopped LLN applied to score outer products, followed by the same Taylor
 205: bound and continuity of matrix inversion on the uniformly positive-definite
 206: set, proves information consistency.  The normalization and the two
 207: stationary endpoint scores obey the same conclusion: their parameter
 208: increments are bounded by \(N^{-1/2}\) times a polynomial in
 209: \(\max(A_N,R_N)\), which is \(O_P(\log N)\) by \textup{(U6)}.  Thus they
 210: contribute \(o_P(1)\) uniformly to the plug-in difference.  Contiguity
 211: transfers every null \(o_P(1)\) assertion to bounded local alternatives.
 212: \end{proof}
 213: 
 214: \begin{lemma}[Two-point threshold-risk lower bound]
 215: \label{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}
 216: Fix a collision base \((\eta_0,0)\), hold \(\eta_0\) fixed, and compare
 217: \(P_{0,N}=P_{\eta_0,0}^{(N)}\) with
 218: \(P_{1,N}=P_{\eta_0,v_0/\sqrt N}^{(N)}\), where \(v_0>0\).  Let
 219: \(\mathcal R_{i,N}\) be their unordered rate multisets.  Then
 220: \[
 221:  d_{\rm m}(\mathcal R_{0,N},\mathcal R_{1,N})
 222:  =\sqrt{v_0}\,N^{-1/4},
 223: \tag{U13}
 224: \]
 225: and, for every \(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\),
 226: \[
 227:  \liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat{\mathcal R}_N}
 228:  \max_{i=0,1}P_{i,N}\!\left\{
 229:  N^{1/4}d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N,\mathcal R_{i,N})>a
 230:  \right\}
 231:  \ge \Phi_{\rm N}\!\left(
 232:  -\frac{v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}}2\right)>0.
 233: \tag{U14}
 234: \]
 235: Thus the lower conclusion is pointwise at a fixed base, uses two alternatives
 236: and threshold loss, and asserts optimality in rate rather than an exact
 237: minimax-risk theorem over a continuum of local parameters.
 238: \end{lemma}
 239: 
 240: \begin{proof}
 241: The two balls of radius \(aN^{-1/4}\) around the candidates are disjoint by
 242: \textup{(U13)}.  Assigning an estimate to its nearer candidate therefore
 243: turns simultaneous success of an estimator into correct testing of
 244: \(P_{0,N}\) against \(P_{1,N}\).  The LAN likelihood ratio under \(P_{0,N}\)
 245: converges to
 246: \[
 247:  \exp\{v_0Z-\tfrac12v_0^2I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)\},
 248:  \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)).
 249: \tag{U15}
 250: \]
 251: Its limit has mean one; mutual contiguity makes the likelihood ratios uniformly
 252: integrable, so their total-variation distances converge to that of the two
 253: Gaussian shifts separated by
 254: \(v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}\).  For any test, its maximum error is at
 255: least its equal-prior average error, whose limiting infimum is
 256: \(\Phi_{\rm N}\{-v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}/2\}\).  Taking a
 257: measurable estimator within \(o(1)\) of the infimum at each \(N\) proves
 258: \textup{(U14)}.  Strict positivity also follows directly from mutual
 259: contiguity, but \textup{(U14)} records the quantitative Gaussian bound.
 260: \end{proof}

  33: def _analytic_h_and_derivative(w: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
  34:     """Return H(w) and H'(w) on the real analytic branch w < 1."""
  35:     if not math.isfinite(w) or w >= 1.0:
  36:         raise ValueError("w must be finite and less than one")
  37:     if abs(w) < 1e-6:
  38:         value = 1.0 - w / 3.0 - 4.0 * w**2 / 45.0 - 44.0 * w**3 / 945.0
  39:         derivative = -1.0 / 3.0 - 8.0 * w / 45.0 - 44.0 * w**2 / 315.0
  40:         return value, derivative
  41:     if w > 0.0:
  42:         root = math.sqrt(w)
  43:         angle = math.atanh(root)
  44:         value = root / angle
  45:         derivative = (angle - root / (1.0 - root**2)) / (
  46:             2.0 * root * angle**2
  47:         )
  48:         return value, derivative
  49:     root = math.sqrt(-w)
  50:     angle = math.atan(root)
  51:     value = root / angle
  52:     derivative = -(angle - root / (1.0 + root**2)) / (
  53:         2.0 * root * angle**2
  54:     )
  55:     return value, derivative

  58: def analytic_log_divided_difference(sigma1: float, sigma2: float) -> float:
  59:     """Evaluate the real analytic continuation in symmetric coordinates."""
  60:     if not (math.isfinite(sigma1) and math.isfinite(sigma2)):
  61:         raise ValueError("symmetric coordinates must be finite")
  62:     if sigma1 <= 0.0 or sigma2 <= 0.0:
  63:         raise ValueError("sigma1 and sigma2 must be positive")
  64:     w = 1.0 - 4.0 * sigma2 / sigma1**2
  65:     h, _ = _analytic_h_and_derivative(w)
  66:     return 0.5 * sigma1 * (1.0 - 0.5 * math.log(sigma2) * h)
  67: 
  68: 
  69: def _analytic_log_divided_difference_gradient(
  70:     sigma1: float, sigma2: float
  71: ) -> FloatArray:
  72:     w = 1.0 - 4.0 * sigma2 / sigma1**2
  73:     h, h_prime = _analytic_h_and_derivative(w)
  74:     log_sigma2 = math.log(sigma2)
  75:     dw_dsigma1 = 8.0 * sigma2 / sigma1**3
  76:     dw_dsigma2 = -4.0 / sigma1**2
  77:     common = 1.0 - 0.5 * log_sigma2 * h
  78:     d_sigma1 = 0.5 * common - 0.25 * sigma1 * log_sigma2 * h_prime * dw_dsigma1
  79:     d_sigma2 = -0.25 * sigma1 * (
  80:         h / sigma2 + log_sigma2 * h_prime * dw_dsigma2
  81:     )
  82:     return np.array([d_sigma1, d_sigma2])

  85: def constraint_jacobian(coordinates: ArrayLike) -> FloatArray:
  86:     """Return the Jacobian of (analytic image residual, discriminant)."""
  87:     r0, r1, r2 = np.asarray(coordinates, dtype=float)
  88:     denominator = r1 - r0**2
  89:     if r0 <= 0.0 or denominator == 0.0:
  90:         raise ValueError("coordinates lie outside the quotient chart")
  91:     a = r1 / r0
  92:     lam = (r2 - r0**2) / denominator
  93:     sigma1 = 1.0 - a + lam
  94:     sigma2 = r0 * (1.0 - lam) - a + lam
  95:     da = np.array([-r1 / r0**2, 1.0 / r0, 0.0])
  96:     dlam = np.array(
  97:         [2.0 * r0 * (lam - 1.0) / denominator, -lam / denominator, 1.0 / denominator]
  98:     )
  99:     dphi1 = -da + dlam
 100:     dphi2 = np.array([1.0 - lam, 0.0, 0.0]) - da + (1.0 - r0) * dlam
 101:     dphi = np.vstack([dphi1, dphi2])
 102:     gradient = _analytic_log_divided_difference_gradient(sigma1, sigma2)
 103:     de = da + gradient @ dphi
 104:     ddiscriminant = np.array([2.0 * sigma1, -4.0]) @ dphi
 105:     return np.vstack([de, ddiscriminant])

 108: def _gap_masses(x: float, y: float, tolerance: float = 1e-15) -> FloatArray:
 109:     masses: list[float] = []
 110:     p = math.exp(-x)
 111:     s = math.exp(-y)
 112: 
 113:     def survival(k: int) -> float:
 114:         if math.isclose(x, y, rel_tol=1e-10, abs_tol=1e-14):
 115:             theta = 0.5 * (x + y)
 116:             return math.exp(-theta * k) * (1.0 + theta * k)
 117:         return (y * p**k - x * s**k) / (y - x)
 118: 
 119:     previous = survival(0)
 120:     for k in range(1_000_000):
 121:         following = survival(k + 1)
 122:         masses.append(previous - following)
 123:         if following < tolerance:
 124:             return np.asarray(masses)
 125:         previous = following
 126:     raise ArithmeticError("gap-law truncation did not converge")
 127: 
 128: 
 129: def survival_factor_gap_masses(p: float, s: float, maximum_gap: int) -> FloatArray:
 130:     """Return gap masses 0,...,maximum_gap-1 from survival factors p and s."""
 131:     if not (0.0 < p < 1.0 and 0.0 < s < 1.0):
 132:         raise ValueError("p and s must lie in (0,1)")
 133:     if maximum_gap < 1:
 134:         raise ValueError("maximum_gap must be positive")
 135:     x = -math.log(p)
 136:     y = -math.log(s)
 137:     indices = np.arange(maximum_gap + 1, dtype=float)
 138:     if math.isclose(x, y, rel_tol=1e-10, abs_tol=1e-14):
 139:         rate = 0.5 * (x + y)
 140:         survival = np.exp(-rate * indices) * (1.0 + rate * indices)
 141:     else:
 142:         survival = (y * p**indices - x * s**indices) / (y - x)
 143:     return survival[:-1] - survival[1:]
 144: 
 145: 
 146: def singular_gap_expansion(z: float, maximum_gap: int) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray]:
 147:     """Return g_z(k) and the d^2 coefficient for (p,s)=(z+d,z-d)."""
 148:     if not 0.0 < z < 1.0:
 149:         raise ValueError("z must lie in (0,1)")
 150:     if maximum_gap < 1:
 151:         raise ValueError("maximum_gap must be positive")
 152:     k = np.arange(maximum_gap, dtype=float)
 153:     log_z = math.log(z)
 154:     denominator = 1.0 - z + log_z * (k * z - k + z)
 155:     gap = z**k * denominator
 156:     numerator = (
 157:         k**3 * z * log_z
 158:         - k**3 * log_z
 159:         - 3.0 * k**2 * z
 160:         + 3.0 * k**2 * log_z
 161:         + 3.0 * k**2
 162:         - 3.0 * k * z * log_z
 163:         - 6.0 * k * z
 164:         - 2.0 * z * log_z
 165:         - 3.0 * z
 166:     )
 167:     coefficient = z**k * numerator / (6.0 * z**2)
 168:     return gap, coefficient
 169: 
 170: 
 171: def singular_gap_score(
 172:     z: float, tolerance: float = 1e-15
 173: ) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray, float, float]:
 174:     """Return the diagonal gap law, singular score, cycle mean, and information."""
 175:     if not 0.0 < tolerance < 1.0:
 176:         raise ValueError("tolerance must lie in (0,1)")
 177:     rate = -math.log(z)
 178:     maximum_gap = 1
 179:     while equal_rate_gap_tail(rate, maximum_gap) >= tolerance:
 180:         maximum_gap += 1
 181:         if maximum_gap > 1_000_000:
 182:             raise ArithmeticError("gap-law truncation did not converge")
 183:     gap, coefficient = singular_gap_expansion(z, maximum_gap)
 184:     score = coefficient / gap
 185:     mean_cycle = (1.0 - z - z * math.log(z)) / (1.0 - z) ** 2
 186:     information = float(np.dot(gap, score**2) / mean_cycle)
 187:     return gap, score, mean_cycle, information

 190: def singular_symmetric_shift(z: float, h: float, sample_size: int) -> FloatArray:
 191:     """Return sqrt(N) times the symmetric-coordinate shift of the N^-1/4 split."""
 192:     if not 0.0 < z < 1.0 or not math.isfinite(h):
 193:         raise ValueError("z must lie in (0,1) and h must be finite")
 194:     if sample_size < 1:
 195:         raise ValueError("sample_size must be positive")
 196:     root_n = math.sqrt(sample_size)
 197:     displacement = h / math.sqrt(root_n)
 198:     p = z + displacement
 199:     s = z - displacement
 200:     if not (0.0 < p < 1.0 and 0.0 < s < 1.0):
 201:         raise ValueError("the split survival factors must lie in (0,1)")
 202:     return root_n * np.array([p + s - 2.0 * z, p * s - z**2])

 205: def regenerative_inclusion_covariance(x: float, y: float) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray]:
 206:     """Deterministically sum the complete-cycle covariance from the gap law."""
 207:     if min(x, y) <= 0.0:
 208:         raise ValueError("dimensionless rates must be positive")
 209:     g = _gap_masses(x, y)
 210:     index = np.arange(g.size)
 211:     mu = float(np.dot(index + 1.0, g))
 212:     r = np.array([1.0 / mu, g[0] / mu, (g[1] + g[0] ** 2) / mu])
 213:     i = index[:, None]
 214:     j = index[None, :]
 215:     reward = np.empty((g.size, g.size, 3))
 216:     reward[:, :, 0] = 1.0
 217:     reward[:, :, 1] = i == 0
 218:     reward[:, :, 2] = (i == 1) + ((i == 0) & (j == 0))
 219:     centered = reward - r[None, None, :] * (i[:, :, None] + 1.0)
 220:     pair_mass = g[:, None] * g[None, :]
 221:     variance = np.einsum("ij,ija,ijb->ab", pair_mass, centered, centered)
 222:     future_mean = np.einsum("k,jka->ja", g, centered)
 223:     adjacent = np.einsum("ij,ija,jb->ab", pair_mass, centered, future_mean)
 224:     return r, (variance + adjacent + adjacent.T) / mu
 225: 
 226: 
 227: def cone_wald_distance(e: float, discriminant: float, omega: ArrayLike) -> float:
 228:     """Return the covariance-metric squared distance to {0} x [0,infinity)."""
 229:     covariance = np.asarray(omega, dtype=float)
 230:     if covariance.shape != (2, 2) or np.linalg.eigvalsh(covariance)[0] <= 0.0:
 231:         raise ValueError("omega must be a positive-definite 2 by 2 matrix")
 232:     beta = covariance[0, 1] / covariance[0, 0]
 233:     variance = covariance[1, 1] - covariance[0, 1] ** 2 / covariance[0, 0]
 234:     standardized_inequality = discriminant - beta * e
 235:     return e**2 / covariance[0, 0] + min(standardized_inequality, 0.0) ** 2 / variance
 236: 
 237: 
 238: def _chi_square_cdf(value: float, degrees: int) -> float:
 239:     if value <= 0.0:
 240:         return 0.0
 241:     if degrees == 1:
 242:         return math.erf(math.sqrt(value / 2.0))
 243:     if degrees == 2:
 244:         return 1.0 - math.exp(-value / 2.0)
 245:     raise ValueError("only one and two degrees of freedom are used")
 246: 
 247: 
 248: def boundary_critical_value(alpha: float) -> float:
 249:     """Return the upper-alpha quantile of 0.5 chi1^2 + 0.5 chi2^2."""
 250:     if not 0.0 < alpha < 1.0:
 251:         raise ValueError("alpha must lie in (0,1)")
 252:     lower, upper = 0.0, 1.0
 253:     target = 1.0 - alpha
 254:     while 0.5 * (_chi_square_cdf(upper, 1) + _chi_square_cdf(upper, 2)) < target:
 255:         upper *= 2.0
 256:     for _ in range(80):
 257:         midpoint = 0.5 * (lower + upper)
 258:         cdf = 0.5 * (_chi_square_cdf(midpoint, 1) + _chi_square_cdf(midpoint, 2))
 259:         if cdf < target:
 260:             lower = midpoint
 261:         else:
 262:             upper = midpoint
 263:     return 0.5 * (lower + upper)
 264:

 266: def local_gap_perturbation_basis() -> FloatArray:
 267:     """Rows give the eta_mu, eta_0, eta_1 perturbations on gaps 0,...,3."""
 268:     return np.array(
 269:         [[0.0, 0.0, -1.0, 1.0], [1.0, 0.0, -3.0, 2.0], [0.0, 1.0, -2.0, 1.0]]
 270:     )

 272: 
 273: def local_power(
 274:     delta: float, tau: float, omega: ArrayLike, alpha: float = 0.05
 275: ) -> float:
 276:     """Evaluate the joint image test's two-coordinate local-power integral."""
 277:     covariance = np.asarray(omega, dtype=float)
 278:     beta = covariance[0, 1] / covariance[0, 0]
 279:     variance = covariance[1, 1] - covariance[0, 1] ** 2 / covariance[0, 0]
 280:     a_star = delta / math.sqrt(covariance[0, 0])
 281:     b_star = (tau - beta * delta) / math.sqrt(variance)
 282:     critical = boundary_critical_value(alpha)
 283: 
 284:     with mp.workdps(40):
 285:         root_critical = mp.sqrt(critical)
 286: 
 287:         def normal_cdf(value: mp.mpf) -> mp.mpf:
 288:             return (1 + mp.erf(value / mp.sqrt(2))) / 2
 289: 
 290:         def interval_probability(q: mp.mpf) -> mp.mpf:
 291:             if q <= 0:
 292:                 return mp.mpf("0")
 293:             root = mp.sqrt(q)
 294:             return normal_cdf(root - a_star) - normal_cdf(-root - a_star)
 295: 
 296:         positive_part = normal_cdf(b_star) * interval_probability(critical)
 297:         negative_part = mp.quad(
 298:             lambda value: interval_probability(critical - value**2)
 299:             * mp.exp(-((value - b_star) ** 2) / 2)
 300:             / mp.sqrt(2 * mp.pi),
 301:             [-root_critical, 0],
 302:         )
 303:         return float(1 - positive_part - negative_part)
 304: 
 305: 
 306: def symmetric_log_divided_difference(p: float, s: float) -> float:
 307:     """Return the symmetric logarithmic divided difference C(p,s)."""
 308:     if not (0.0 < p < 1.0 and 0.0 < s < 1.0):
 309:         raise ValueError("p and s must lie in (0,1)")
 310:     if math.isclose(p, s, rel_tol=1e-10, abs_tol=1e-14):
 311:         m = 0.5 * (p + s)
 312:         d = 0.5 * (p - s)
 313:         return (
 314:             m * (1.0 - math.log(m))
 315:             + d**2 / m * (0.5 + math.log(m) / 3.0)
 316:             + d**4 / m**3 * (1.0 / 12.0 + 4.0 * math.log(m) / 45.0)
 317:         )
 318:     return (s * math.log(p) - p * math.log(s)) / (math.log(p) - math.log(s))
 319: 
 320: 
 321: def hidden_mode(x: float, y: float) -> float:
 322:     """Return the continuous secant extension of the hidden eigenvalue."""
 323:     if not (math.isfinite(x) and math.isfinite(y) and x > 0.0 and y > 0.0):
 324:         raise ValueError("x and y must be finite and positive")
 325:     if math.isclose(x, y, rel_tol=1e-10, abs_tol=1e-14):
 326:         midpoint = 0.5 * (x + y)
 327:         return math.exp(-midpoint) * (1.0 - midpoint)
 328:     return (y * math.exp(-y) - x * math.exp(-x)) / (y - x)

 330: 
 331: def markov_gap_alternative(
 332:     diagonal_rate: float, eta: float
 333: ) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray, FloatArray, float]:
 334:     """Construct the finite-range Markov-gap alternative at an exchange point."""
 335:     if not math.isfinite(diagonal_rate) or diagonal_rate <= 0.0:
 336:         raise ValueError("the diagonal rate must be finite and positive")
 337:     if not math.isfinite(eta) or eta < 0.0:
 338:         raise ValueError("eta must be finite and nonnegative")
 339: 
 340:     gap_mass = _gap_masses(diagonal_rate, diagonal_rate)
 341:     gap_mass /= gap_mass.sum()
 342:     if gap_mass.size < 3 or min(gap_mass[1], gap_mass[2]) <= 0.0:
 343:         raise ArithmeticError("the truncated gap law does not contain positive masses 1 and 2")
 344: 
 345:     score = np.zeros_like(gap_mass)
 346:     score[1] = 1.0
 347:     score[2] = -gap_mass[1] / gap_mass[2]
 348:     maximum_eta = gap_mass[2] / gap_mass[1]
 349:     if eta >= maximum_eta:
 350:         raise ValueError(f"eta must be smaller than {maximum_eta:.12g} for positivity")
 351: 
 352:     transition = gap_mass[None, :] * (
 353:         1.0 + eta * score[:, None] * score[None, :]
 354:     )
 355:     indices = np.arange(gap_mass.size, dtype=float)
 356:     mean_cycle = float((indices + 1.0) @ gap_mass)
 357:     return gap_mass, score, transition, mean_cycle
 358: 
 359: 
 360: def markov_gap_inclusions(
 361:     gap_mass: ArrayLike, transition: ArrayLike, mean_cycle: float
 362: ) -> FloatArray:
 363:     """Return the first three inclusion coordinates of a stationary gap chain."""
 364:     g = np.asarray(gap_mass, dtype=float)
 365:     q = np.asarray(transition, dtype=float)
 366:     if g.ndim != 1 or g.size < 2 or q.shape != (g.size, g.size):
 367:         raise ValueError("gap_mass and transition have incompatible shapes")
 368:     if not math.isfinite(mean_cycle) or mean_cycle <= 0.0:
 369:         raise ValueError("mean_cycle must be finite and positive")
 370:     return np.array(
 371:         [
 372:             1.0 / mean_cycle,
 373:             g[0] / mean_cycle,
 374:             (g[1] + g[0] * q[0, 0]) / mean_cycle,
 375:         ]
 376:     )

 378: 
 379: def markov_gap_information(
 380:     gap_mass: ArrayLike, score: ArrayLike, mean_cycle: float
 381: ) -> float:
 382:     """Return Fisher information per calendar bin for the Markov-gap path."""
 383:     g = np.asarray(gap_mass, dtype=float)
 384:     h = np.asarray(score, dtype=float)
 385:     if g.shape != h.shape or g.ndim != 1:
 386:         raise ValueError("gap_mass and score must be one-dimensional arrays of equal size")
 387:     if not math.isfinite(mean_cycle) or mean_cycle <= 0.0:
 388:         raise ValueError("mean_cycle must be finite and positive")
 389:     second_moment = float(g @ (h * h))
 390:     return second_moment**2 / mean_cycle

 392: 
 393: def markov_gap_local_power(
 394:     diagonal_rate: float, local_parameter: float, alpha: float = 0.05
 395: ) -> float:
 396:     """Return the one-sided Gaussian local power of the finite-range score."""
 397:     if not math.isfinite(local_parameter) or local_parameter < 0.0:
 398:         raise ValueError("the local parameter must be finite and nonnegative")
 399:     if not 0.0 < alpha < 1.0:
 400:         raise ValueError("alpha must lie in (0,1)")
 401:     g, h, _, mean_cycle = markov_gap_alternative(diagonal_rate, 0.0)
 402:     information = markov_gap_information(g, h, mean_cycle)
 403:     normal = NormalDist()
 404:     critical = normal.inv_cdf(1.0 - alpha)
 405:     return 1.0 - normal.cdf(critical - local_parameter * math.sqrt(information))

 408: def _probability_vector(gap_mass: ArrayLike) -> FloatArray:
 409:     g = np.asarray(gap_mass, dtype=float)
 410:     if g.ndim != 1 or g.size < 2 or not np.all(np.isfinite(g)):
 411:         raise ValueError("gap_mass must be a finite one-dimensional vector")
 412:     if np.min(g) <= 0.0 or not math.isclose(float(g.sum()), 1.0, abs_tol=1e-12):
 413:         raise ValueError("gap_mass must be a strictly positive probability vector")
 414:     return g

 416: 
 417: def markov_palm_tangent_projection(
 418:     gap_mass: ArrayLike, values: ArrayLike
 419: ) -> FloatArray:
 420:     """Project a finite table onto the fixed-marginal, q(0,0)=0 tangent space."""
 421:     g = _probability_vector(gap_mass)
 422:     table = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
 423:     if table.shape != (g.size, g.size) or not np.all(np.isfinite(table)):
 424:         raise ValueError("values must be a finite square table matching gap_mass")
 425: 
 426:     row_mean = table @ g
 427:     column_mean = g @ table
 428:     interaction = table - row_mean[:, None] - column_mean[None, :] + g @ row_mean
 429:     zero_contrast = np.zeros_like(g)
 430:     zero_contrast[0] = 1.0
 431:     zero_contrast -= g[0]
 432:     atom_interaction = np.outer(zero_contrast, zero_contrast)
 433:     atom_norm_squared = float(
 434:         np.einsum("i,j,ij->", g, g, atom_interaction * atom_interaction)
 435:     )
 436:     coefficient = float(
 437:         np.einsum("i,j,ij->", g, g, interaction * atom_interaction)
 438:         / atom_norm_squared
 439:     )
 440:     return interaction - coefficient * atom_interaction
 441:

 443: def project_markov_tangent(gap_mass: ArrayLike, values: ArrayLike) -> FloatArray:
 444:     """Compatibility alias for :func:`markov_palm_tangent_projection`."""
 445:     return markov_palm_tangent_projection(gap_mass, values)

 448: def markov_palm_transition(
 449:     gap_mass: ArrayLike, score: ArrayLike, parameter: float
 450: ) -> FloatArray:
 451:     """Construct Q(l|k)=g(l){1+parameter*q(k,l)} on a finite gap space."""
 452:     g = _probability_vector(gap_mass)
 453:     q = np.asarray(score, dtype=float)
 454:     if q.shape != (g.size, g.size) or not np.all(np.isfinite(q)):
 455:         raise ValueError("score must be a finite square table matching gap_mass")
 456:     if not math.isfinite(parameter):
 457:         raise ValueError("parameter must be finite")
 458:     transition = g[None, :] * (1.0 + parameter * q)
 459:     if np.min(transition) < -1e-14:
 460:         raise ValueError("parameter makes the transition kernel negative")
 461:     return transition

 463: 
 464: def markov_palm_information(gap_mass: ArrayLike, score: ArrayLike) -> float:
 465:     """Return the fixed-marginal Markov score information per calendar bin."""
 466:     g = _probability_vector(gap_mass)
 467:     q = np.asarray(score, dtype=float)
 468:     if q.shape != (g.size, g.size) or not np.all(np.isfinite(q)):
 469:         raise ValueError("score must be a finite square table matching gap_mass")
 470:     mean_cycle = float((np.arange(g.size, dtype=float) + 1.0) @ g)
 471:     norm_squared = float(np.einsum("i,j,ij->", g, g, q * q))
 472:     return norm_squared / mean_cycle

 474: 
 475: def _weighted_mean_zero_basis(gap_mass: ArrayLike) -> FloatArray:
 476:     g = _probability_vector(gap_mass)
 477:     candidates = []
 478:     zero_contrast = np.zeros_like(g)
 479:     zero_contrast[0] = 1.0
 480:     candidates.append(zero_contrast - g[0])
 481:     for index in range(1, g.size):
 482:         contrast = np.zeros_like(g)
 483:         contrast[index] = 1.0
 484:         candidates.append(contrast - g[index])
 485: 
 486:     basis: list[FloatArray] = []
 487:     for candidate in candidates:
 488:         residual = candidate.copy()
 489:         for vector in basis:
 490:             residual -= float(g @ (residual * vector)) * vector
 491:         norm = math.sqrt(float(g @ (residual * residual)))
 492:         if norm > 2e-12:
 493:             basis.append(residual / norm)
 494:         if len(basis) == g.size - 1:
 495:             break
 496:     return np.asarray(basis)
 497:

 499: def finite_markov_tangent_basis(gap_mass: ArrayLike) -> FloatArray:
 500:     """Return an orthonormal basis of the finite Markov-Palm tangent space."""
 501:     one_gap_basis = _weighted_mean_zero_basis(gap_mass)
 502:     products = [
 503:         np.outer(left, right)
 504:         for left_index, left in enumerate(one_gap_basis)
 505:         for right_index, right in enumerate(one_gap_basis)
 506:         if (left_index, right_index) != (0, 0)
 507:     ]
 508:     return np.asarray(products)

 511: def equal_rate_gap_tail(rate: float, layer: int) -> float:
 512:     """Return S_layer=exp(-rate*layer)*(1+rate*layer)."""
 513:     if not math.isfinite(rate) or rate <= 0.0 or layer < 0:
 514:         raise ValueError("rate must be positive and layer must be nonnegative")
 515:     return math.exp(-rate * layer) * (1.0 + rate * layer)

 517: 
 518: def weighted_helmert_partition(rate: float, layer: int) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray]:
 519:     """Evaluate e_0,...,e_layer on atoms 0,...,layer and the residual tail."""
 520:     if layer < 0:
 521:         raise ValueError("layer must be nonnegative")
 522:     tails = np.array([equal_rate_gap_tail(rate, j) for j in range(layer + 2)])
 523:     masses = tails[:-1] - tails[1:]
 524:     partition_mass = np.concatenate((masses, tails[-1:]))
 525:     basis = np.zeros((layer + 1, layer + 2))
 526:     for index in range(layer + 1):
 527:         basis[index, index] = math.sqrt(
 528:             tails[index + 1] / (masses[index] * tails[index])
 529:         )
 530:         basis[index, index + 1 :] = -math.sqrt(
 531:             masses[index] / (tails[index] * tails[index + 1])
 532:         )
 533:     return partition_mass, basis

 535: 
 536: def helmert_layer_diagnostics(rate: float, layer: int) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
 537:     """Return Gram error, S_J-scaled tensor envelope, and scaled third moment."""
 538:     partition_mass, basis = weighted_helmert_partition(rate, layer)
 539:     gram = np.einsum("k,ak,bk->ab", partition_mass, basis, basis)
 540:     tensor_envelope = 0.0
 541:     for left in range(layer + 1):
 542:         for right in range(layer + 1):
 543:             if (left, right) != (0, 0):
 544:                 tensor_envelope = max(
 545:                     tensor_envelope,
 546:                     float(np.max(np.abs(np.outer(basis[left], basis[right])))),
 547:                 )
 548: 
 549:     christoffel = np.sum(basis * basis, axis=0)
 550:     omitted = np.outer(basis[0] * basis[0], basis[0] * basis[0])
 551:     vector_norm_squared = np.outer(christoffel, christoffel) - omitted
 552:     vector_third_moment = float(
 553:         np.einsum(
 554:             "i,j,ij->",
 555:             partition_mass,
 556:             partition_mass,
 557:             np.maximum(vector_norm_squared, 0.0) ** 1.5,
 558:         )
 559:     )
 560:     tail = equal_rate_gap_tail(rate, layer)
 561:     return (
 562:         float(np.max(np.abs(gram - np.eye(layer + 1)))),
 563:         tail * tensor_envelope,
 564:         tail * vector_third_moment,
 565:     )

 567: 
 568: def _helmert_interaction_values(rate: float, layer: int) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray]:
 569:     partition_mass, basis = weighted_helmert_partition(rate, layer)
 570:     values = np.asarray(
 571:         [
 572:             np.outer(basis[:, left], basis[:, right]).reshape(-1)[1:]
 573:             for left in range(partition_mass.size)
 574:             for right in range(partition_mass.size)
 575:         ]
 576:     ).reshape(partition_mass.size, partition_mass.size, -1)
 577:     return partition_mass, values

 580: def helmert_overlap_diagnostics(rate: float, layer: int) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
 581:     """Return covariance error, lag-one covariance error, and S_J-scaled third moment."""
 582:     partition_mass, values = _helmert_interaction_values(rate, layer)
 583:     dimension = (layer + 1) ** 2 - 1
 584:     covariance = np.einsum(
 585:         "i,j,ija,ijb->ab", partition_mass, partition_mass, values, values
 586:     )
 587:     lag_covariance = np.einsum(
 588:         "i,j,k,ija,jkb->ab",
 589:         partition_mass,
 590:         partition_mass,
 591:         partition_mass,
 592:         values,
 593:         values,
 594:     )
 595:     third_moment = float(
 596:         np.einsum(
 597:             "i,j,ij->",
 598:             partition_mass,
 599:             partition_mass,
 600:             np.linalg.norm(values, axis=2) ** 3,
 601:         )
 602:     )
 603:     return (
 604:         float(np.max(np.abs(covariance - np.eye(dimension)))),
 605:         float(np.max(np.abs(lag_covariance))),
 606:         equal_rate_gap_tail(rate, layer) * third_moment,
 607:     )

 610: def helmert_exact_block_moment_ratio(rate: float, layer: int, length: int) -> float:
 611:     """Enumerate a small overlap block and divide its third moment by its Rosenthal scale."""
 612:     if length < 1:
 613:         raise ValueError("length must be positive")
 614:     partition_mass, values = _helmert_interaction_values(rate, layer)
 615:     dimension = values.shape[2]
 616:     third_moment = 0.0
 617:     for states in itertools.product(range(partition_mass.size), repeat=length + 1):
 618:         probability = math.prod(float(partition_mass[state]) for state in states)
 619:         block_sum = np.zeros(dimension)
 620:         for index in range(length):
 621:             block_sum += values[states[index], states[index + 1]]
 622:         third_moment += probability * float(np.linalg.norm(block_sum) ** 3)
 623:     scale = (length * dimension) ** 1.5 + length / equal_rate_gap_tail(rate, layer)
 624:     return third_moment / scale

 627: def helmert_blocking_log_terms(
 628:     rate: float, log_sample_size: float, layer: int
 629: ) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
 630:     """Return deleted-edge and CMU dimension-adjusted log error bounds."""
 631:     dimension = (layer + 1) ** 2 - 1
 632:     log_block_length = math.log(dimension**2 + log_sample_size)
 633:     log_dimension = math.log(dimension)
 634:     log_tail = -rate * layer + math.log1p(rate * layer)
 635:     deleted_mean_square = math.exp(log_dimension - log_block_length) + math.exp(
 636:         log_block_length + log_dimension - log_sample_size
 637:     )
 638:     return (
 639:         math.log(deleted_mean_square),
 640:         0.5 * log_block_length + 2.5 * log_dimension - 0.5 * log_sample_size,
 641:         log_dimension - 0.5 * log_sample_size - log_tail,
 642:     )

 645: def helmert_zolotarev_blocking_log_terms(
 646:     rate: float, log_sample_size: float, layer: int
 647: ) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
 648:     """Return deleted-edge and actual-block log terms for the Z2--W2 bound."""
 649:     dimension = (layer + 1) ** 2 - 1
 650:     log_block_length = math.log(dimension**2 + log_sample_size)
 651:     log_dimension = math.log(dimension)
 652:     log_tail = -rate * layer + math.log1p(rate * layer)
 653:     deleted_mean_square = math.exp(log_dimension - log_block_length) + math.exp(
 654:         log_block_length + log_dimension - log_sample_size
 655:     )
 656:     return (
 657:         math.log(deleted_mean_square),
 658:         0.5 * log_block_length + 1.5 * log_dimension - 0.5 * log_sample_size,
 659:         -0.5 * log_sample_size - log_tail,

 663: def helmert_critical_log_mean(rate: float, layer: int, constant: float) -> float:
 664:     """Return log(n*S_J^2) on 2*rate*J=log n+2*log log n-constant."""
 665:     target = 2.0 * rate * layer + constant
 666:     lower = 1.0
 667:     upper = max(2.0, target)
 668:     while upper + 2.0 * math.log(upper) < target:
 669:         upper *= 2.0
 670:     for _ in range(100):
 671:         midpoint = 0.5 * (lower + upper)
 672:         if midpoint + 2.0 * math.log(midpoint) < target:
 673:             lower = midpoint
 674:         else:
 675:             upper = midpoint
 676:     log_sample_size = 0.5 * (lower + upper)
 677:     log_tail = -rate * layer + math.log1p(rate * layer)
 678:     return log_sample_size + 2.0 * log_tail

 681: def helmert_log_rate_terms(rate: float, log_sample_size: float, layer: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
 682:     """Return logs of n*S_J^2 and d_J/(sqrt(n)*S_J)."""
 683:     if not math.isfinite(log_sample_size):
 684:         raise ValueError("log_sample_size must be finite")
 685:     log_tail = -rate * layer + math.log1p(rate * layer)
 686:     dimension = (layer + 1) ** 2 - 1
 687:     return (
 688:         log_sample_size + 2.0 * log_tail,
 689:         math.log(dimension) - 0.5 * log_sample_size - log_tail,
 690:     )

 692: 
 693: def weighted_omnibus_monte_carlo(
 694:     weights: ArrayLike,
 695:     direction: ArrayLike,
 696:     alpha: float = 0.05,
 697:     draws: int = 100_000,
 698:     seed: int = 0,
 699: ) -> tuple[float, float]:
 700:     """Numerically compare the weighted Gaussian score law at zero and a direction."""
 701:     lam = np.asarray(weights, dtype=float)
 702:     shift = np.asarray(direction, dtype=float)
 703:     if lam.ndim != 1 or shift.shape != lam.shape or np.min(lam) <= 0.0:
 704:         raise ValueError("weights and direction must be equal-length vectors with positive weights")
 705:     if not 0.0 < alpha < 1.0 or draws < 2:
 706:         raise ValueError("alpha and draws are outside their admissible ranges")
 707:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
 708:     normals = rng.normal(size=(draws, lam.size))
 709:     null_values = (normals * normals) @ lam
 710:     critical = float(np.quantile(null_values, 1.0 - alpha))
 711:     alternative_values = ((normals + shift) ** 2) @ lam
 712:     return (
 713:         float(np.mean(null_values > critical)),
 714:         float(np.mean(alternative_values > critical)),
 715:     )
 716: 
 717: 
 718: def rademacher_mixture_second_moment(
 719:     radius: float, mean_cycle: float, dimension: int
 720: ) -> float:
 721:     """Return [cosh(r^2/(mu*d))]^d for the Gaussian-sequence mixture."""
 722:     if radius <= 0.0 or mean_cycle <= 0.0 or dimension < 1:
 723:         raise ValueError("radius, mean_cycle, and dimension must be positive")
 724:     argument = radius * radius / (mean_cycle * dimension)
 725:     return math.exp(dimension * math.log(math.cosh(argument)))
 726: 
 727: 
 728: def sampled_counter_inclusions(x: float, y: float) -> FloatArray:
 729:     """Return (r0,r1,r2) for dimensionless positive rates x and y."""
 730:     with mp.workdps(50):
 731:         x_mp = mp.mpf(x)
 732:         y_mp = mp.mpf(y)
 733:         p = mp.exp(-x_mp)
 734:         s = mp.exp(-y_mp)
 735:         if mp.almosteq(x_mp, y_mp):
 736:             b = x_mp * p
 737:         else:
 738:             b = y_mp * (p - s) / (y_mp - x_mp)
 739:         a = 1 - s - b
 740:         rho = (1 - p) * (1 - s) / (1 - p + b)
 741:         lam = p - b
 742:         r1 = rho * a
 743:         r2 = rho * rho + lam * (r1 - rho * rho)
 744:         return np.array([rho, r1, r2], dtype=object)
 745: 
 746: 
 747: def physical_image_residual(coordinates: ArrayLike) -> float:
 748:     """Evaluate the exact sampled-counter image residual E(r)."""
 749:     with mp.workdps(50):
 750:         r0, r1, r2 = (mp.mpf(value) for value in coordinates)
 751:         if r0 <= 0:
 752:             raise ValueError("r0 must be positive")
 753:         denominator = r1 - r0 * r0
 754:         if denominator == 0:
 755:             raise ValueError("the quotient denominator must be nonzero")
 756:         a = r1 / r0
 757:         lam = (r2 - r0 * r0) / denominator
 758:         sigma1 = 1 - a + lam
 759:         sigma2 = r0 * (1 - lam) - a + lam
 760:         discriminant = sigma1 * sigma1 - 4 * sigma2
 761:         if discriminant < mp.mpf("-2e-40"):
 762:             raise ValueError("the quotient polynomial does not have real roots")
 763:         root_gap = mp.sqrt(max(discriminant, 0))
 764:         p = (sigma1 + root_gap) / 2
 765:         s = (sigma1 - root_gap) / 2
 766:         if mp.almosteq(p, s):
 767:             divided_difference = p * (1 - mp.log(p))
 768:         else:
 769:             divided_difference = (s * mp.log(p) - p * mp.log(s)) / (
 770:                 mp.log(p) - mp.log(s)
 771:             )
 772:         return float(a - 1 + divided_difference)
 773: 
 774: 
 775: def rounded_cycle_mean(gamma: float, kappa: float, delta: float) -> float:
 776:     """Return E ceil((Exp(kappa)+Exp(gamma))/delta)."""
 777:     if min(gamma, kappa, delta) <= 0.0:
 778:         raise ValueError("gamma, kappa, and delta must be positive")
 779:     x = gamma * delta
 780:     y = kappa * delta
 781:     if math.isclose(gamma, kappa, rel_tol=1e-10, abs_tol=1e-14):
 782:         p = math.exp(-0.5 * (x + y))
 783:         theta = 0.5 * (x + y)
 784:         return 1.0 / (1.0 - p) + theta * p / (1.0 - p) ** 2
 785:     return (
 786:         kappa / (-math.expm1(-x)) - gamma / (-math.expm1(-y))
 787:     ) / (kappa - gamma)
 788: 
 789: 
 790: def rounded_cycle_mean_from_tails(
 791:     gamma: float, kappa: float, delta: float, tolerance: float = 1e-16
 792: ) -> float:
 793:     """Independently sum the sampled hypoexponential survival probabilities."""
 794:     x = gamma * delta
 795:     y = kappa * delta
 796:     p = math.exp(-x)
 797:     s = math.exp(-y)
 798:     total = 0.0
 799:     for lag in range(1_000_000):
 800:         if math.isclose(x, y, rel_tol=1e-10, abs_tol=1e-14):
 801:             theta = 0.5 * (x + y)
 802:             tail = math.exp(-theta * lag) * (1.0 + theta * lag)
 803:         else:
 804:             tail = (y * p**lag - x * s**lag) / (y - x)
 805:         total += tail
 806:         if lag > 0 and tail < tolerance:
 807:             return total
 808:     raise ArithmeticError("tail sum did not converge")
 809:

import math
import unittest

import numpy as np

from artifacts import verify_A8_results as verify


class PhysicalImageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_physical_parameter_grid_has_zero_image_residual(self):
        for x in np.geomspace(0.02, 8.0, 24):
            for y in np.geomspace(0.03, 9.0, 23):
                coordinates = verify.sampled_counter_inclusions(float(x), float(y))
                self.assertLess(abs(verify.physical_image_residual(coordinates)), 2e-12)

    def test_symmetric_log_divided_difference_is_regular_on_diagonal(self):
        for m in (0.15, 0.35, 0.5, 0.8):
            for d in (1e-2, 4e-3, 1e-3):
                exact = verify.symmetric_log_divided_difference(m + d, m - d)
                second_order = m * (1.0 - math.log(m)) + d**2 / m * (
                    0.5 + math.log(m) / 3.0
                )
                self.assertLess(abs(exact - second_order), 3.0 * d**4 / m**3)

    def test_analytic_extension_matches_real_root_formula(self):
        for p, s in ((0.12, 0.83), (0.35, 0.5), (0.6, 0.600001)):
            expected = verify.symmetric_log_divided_difference(p, s)
            actual = verify.analytic_log_divided_difference(p + s, p * s)
            self.assertAlmostEqual(actual, expected, places=11)

    def test_analytic_extension_is_real_on_nonreal_root_side(self):
        value = verify.analytic_log_divided_difference(1.0, 0.3)
        self.assertTrue(math.isfinite(value))

    def test_joint_constraint_jacobian_has_rank_two_on_grid(self):
        for x in np.geomspace(0.1, 5.0, 12):
            for y in np.geomspace(0.1, 5.5, 11):
                coordinates = verify.sampled_counter_inclusions(float(x), float(y))
                jacobian = verify.constraint_jacobian(coordinates)
                self.assertGreater(np.linalg.svd(jacobian, compute_uv=False)[-1], 1e-5)


class JointImageTestChecks(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_regenerative_covariance_and_constraint_covariance_are_positive(self):
        for x, y in ((0.1, 0.1), (0.2, 1.7), (1.0, 1.0), (2.0, 4.0), (5.0, 5.5)):
            coordinates, sigma_r = verify.regenerative_inclusion_covariance(x, y)
            jacobian = verify.constraint_jacobian(coordinates)
            omega = jacobian @ sigma_r @ jacobian.T
            self.assertGreater(np.linalg.eigvalsh(sigma_r)[0], 1e-8)
            self.assertGreater(np.linalg.eigvalsh(omega)[0], 1e-8)

    def test_cone_distance_matches_direct_scalar_minimization(self):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(20260803)
        for _ in range(200):
            matrix = rng.normal(size=(2, 2))
            omega = matrix @ matrix.T + 0.1 * np.eye(2)
            e, d = rng.normal(size=2)
            beta = omega[0, 1] / omega[0, 0]
            minimizer = max(0.0, d - beta * e)
            residual = np.array([e, d - minimizer])
            direct = residual @ np.linalg.inv(omega) @ residual
            self.assertAlmostEqual(
                verify.cone_wald_distance(e, d, omega), direct, places=11
            )

    def test_boundary_critical_value_matches_mixture_quantile(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(verify.boundary_critical_value(0.05), 5.1383807853, places=9)

    def test_finite_support_submodel_has_prescribed_coordinate_changes(self):
        directions = verify.local_gap_perturbation_basis()
        cycle_lengths = np.arange(1.0, 5.0)
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(directions.sum(axis=1), 0.0))
        self.assertTrue(
            np.allclose(directions @ cycle_lengths, np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0]))
        )
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(directions[:, 0], np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])))
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(directions[:, 1], np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0])))

    def test_local_power_is_size_at_origin_and_increases_nonreal_side(self):
        omega = np.array([[1.4, 0.3], [0.3, 1.1]])
        alpha = 0.05
        at_origin = verify.local_power(0.0, 0.0, omega, alpha)
        nonreal_side = verify.local_power(0.0, -1.0, omega, alpha)
        physical_side = verify.local_power(0.0, 1.0, omega, alpha)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(at_origin, alpha, places=8)
        self.assertGreater(nonreal_side, alpha)
        self.assertLess(physical_side, alpha)


class HiddenModeTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_sharp_global_spectral_bound_and_extremizer(self):
        lower = -math.exp(-2.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(verify.hidden_mode(2.0, 2.0), lower, places=14)
        for x in np.geomspace(1e-4, 40.0, 160):
            for y in np.geomspace(2e-4, 35.0, 80):
                value = verify.hidden_mode(float(x), float(y))
                self.assertGreaterEqual(value, lower - 2e-14)
                self.assertLess(value, 1.0)

    def test_oracle_one_dependence_equation_has_diagonal_counterexample(self):
        x = y = 2.0
        self.assertAlmostEqual(x * math.exp(-x), y * math.exp(-y), places=15)
        self.assertNotEqual(verify.hidden_mode(x, y), 0.0)


class CompleteVisibleLawTestChecks(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_markov_gap_alternative_is_stochastic_and_preserves_gap_marginal(self):
        for x in (0.35, 1.0, 2.4, 5.0):
            g, h, transition, _ = verify.markov_gap_alternative(x, 0.005)
            self.assertGreaterEqual(np.min(transition), 0.0)
            self.assertTrue(np.allclose(transition.sum(axis=1), 1.0, atol=2e-13))
            self.assertTrue(np.allclose(g @ transition, g, atol=2e-13))
            self.assertAlmostEqual(float(g @ h), 0.0, places=13)
            self.assertEqual(h[0], 0.0)

    def test_markov_gap_alternative_preserves_three_inclusions_but_changes_word_five(self):
        x = 1.35
        null = verify.markov_gap_alternative(x, 0.0)
        alternative = verify.markov_gap_alternative(x, 0.08)
        r_null = verify.markov_gap_inclusions(null[0], null[2], null[3])
        r_alternative = verify.markov_gap_inclusions(
            alternative[0], alternative[2], alternative[3]
        )
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(r_null, r_alternative, atol=2e-13))

        g, _, transition, mu = alternative
        observed = g[1] * transition[1, 1] / mu
        expected = g[1] ** 2 * 1.08 / mu
        self.assertAlmostEqual(observed, expected, places=13)
        self.assertGreater(observed, null[0][1] * null[2][1, 1] / null[3])

    def test_markov_gap_information_matches_score_variance_per_calendar_time(self):
        for x in (0.35, 1.0, 2.4, 5.0):
            g, h, _, mu = verify.markov_gap_alternative(x, 0.0)
            information = verify.markov_gap_information(g, h, mu)
            second_moment = float(g @ (h * h))
            expected = second_moment**2 / mu
            self.assertAlmostEqual(information, expected, places=13)
            self.assertGreater(information, 0.0)

    def test_markov_gap_local_power_has_size_at_origin_and_is_strictly_increasing(self):
        alpha = 0.05
        powers = [verify.markov_gap_local_power(1.35, t, alpha) for t in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0)]
        self.assertAlmostEqual(powers[0], alpha, places=13)
        self.assertGreater(powers[1], powers[0])
        self.assertGreater(powers[2], powers[1])


class CompleteMarkovPalmTangentChecks(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.g = np.array([0.18, 0.27, 0.31, 0.24])
        self.raw = np.array(
            [
                [0.7, -0.3, 0.2, 0.5],
                [-0.8, 0.4, 0.1, -0.6],
                [0.3, 0.9, -0.5, 0.2],
                [-0.2, 0.6, 0.8, -0.7],
            ]
        )

    def test_tangent_projection_is_double_centered_and_annihilates_zero_cell(self):
        score = verify.markov_palm_tangent_projection(self.g, self.raw)
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(score @ self.g, 0.0, atol=2e-14))
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(self.g @ score, 0.0, atol=2e-14))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(score[0, 0], 0.0, places=14)
        self.assertTrue(
            np.allclose(
                verify.markov_palm_tangent_projection(self.g, score),
                score,
                atol=2e-14,
            )
        )

    def test_projected_path_preserves_marginal_and_three_inclusions(self):
        score = verify.markov_palm_tangent_projection(self.g, self.raw)
        transition = verify.markov_palm_transition(self.g, score, 0.08)
        null_transition = np.broadcast_to(self.g, transition.shape)
        mean_cycle = float((np.arange(self.g.size) + 1.0) @ self.g)
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(transition.sum(axis=1), 1.0, atol=2e-14))
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(self.g @ transition, self.g, atol=2e-14))
        self.assertTrue(
            np.allclose(
                verify.markov_gap_inclusions(self.g, transition, mean_cycle),
                verify.markov_gap_inclusions(self.g, null_transition, mean_cycle),
                atol=2e-14,
            )
        )

    def test_calendar_time_information_has_mu_inverse_scaling(self):
        score = verify.markov_palm_tangent_projection(self.g, self.raw)
        mean_cycle = float((np.arange(self.g.size) + 1.0) @ self.g)
        norm_squared = float(np.einsum("i,j,ij->", self.g, self.g, score**2))
        information = verify.markov_palm_information(self.g, score)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(information, norm_squared / mean_cycle, places=14)

    def test_weighted_omnibus_has_strict_power_for_nonzero_direction(self):
        weights = np.array([0.5, 0.2, 0.08, 0.03])
        null_size, alternative_power = verify.weighted_omnibus_monte_carlo(
            weights,
            np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.4, 0.0]),
            alpha=0.05,
            draws=300_000,
            seed=20260807,
        )
        self.assertLess(abs(null_size - 0.05), 0.002)
        self.assertGreater(alternative_power, null_size + 0.01)

    def test_full_markov_tangent_projection_satisfies_all_constraints(self):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(20260807)
        for x in (0.35, 1.0, 2.4, 5.0):
            g = verify.markov_gap_alternative(x, 0.0)[0][:12]
            g /= g.sum()
            projected = verify.markov_palm_tangent_projection(
                g, rng.normal(size=(g.size, g.size))
            )
            self.assertTrue(np.allclose(projected @ g, 0.0, atol=3e-13))
            self.assertTrue(np.allclose(g @ projected, 0.0, atol=3e-13))
            self.assertAlmostEqual(projected[0, 0], 0.0, places=12)

            mean_cycle = float((np.arange(g.size) + 1.0) @ g)
            scale = 0.02 / np.max(np.abs(projected))
            transition = g[None, :] * (1.0 + scale * projected)
            null_transition = np.broadcast_to(g, transition.shape)
            self.assertGreater(np.min(transition), 0.0)
            self.assertTrue(np.allclose(transition.sum(axis=1), 1.0, atol=3e-13))
            self.assertTrue(np.allclose(g @ transition, g, atol=3e-13))
            self.assertTrue(
                np.allclose(
                    verify.markov_gap_inclusions(g, transition, mean_cycle),
                    verify.markov_gap_inclusions(g, null_transition, mean_cycle),
                    atol=3e-13,
                )
            )

    def test_finite_markov_tangent_basis_is_orthonormal_and_complete(self):
        g = verify.markov_gap_alternative(1.35, 0.0)[0][:7]
        g /= g.sum()
        basis = verify.finite_markov_tangent_basis(g)
        self.assertEqual(basis.shape, ((g.size - 1) ** 2 - 1, g.size, g.size))
        gram = np.einsum("i,j,aij,bij->ab", g, g, basis, basis)
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(gram, np.eye(basis.shape[0]), atol=4e-13))
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(np.einsum("aij,j->ai", basis, g), 0.0, atol=3e-13))
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(np.einsum("i,aij->aj", g, basis), 0.0, atol=3e-13))
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(basis[:, 0, 0], 0.0, atol=3e-13))

    def test_markov_tangent_information_and_mixture_limit(self):
        g = verify.markov_gap_alternative(1.35, 0.0)[0][:9]
        g /= g.sum()
        q = verify.finite_markov_tangent_basis(g)[3]
        mean_cycle = float((np.arange(g.size) + 1.0) @ g)
        information = verify.markov_palm_information(g, q)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(information, 1.0 / mean_cycle, places=12)

        lag_covariance = np.einsum("i,j,k,ij,jk->", g, g, g, q, q)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(float(lag_covariance), 0.0, places=12)
        second_moments = [
            verify.rademacher_mixture_second_moment(1.7, mean_cycle, dimension)
            for dimension in (16, 64, 256, 1024)
        ]
        self.assertTrue(all(value > 1.0 for value in second_moments))
        self.assertTrue(all(a > b for a, b in zip(second_moments, second_moments[1:])))
        self.assertLess(second_moments[-1] - 1.0, 3e-3)

    def test_double_centering_cancels_first_order_marginal_drift(self):
        g = np.array([0.12, 0.19, 0.27, 0.23, 0.19])
        q = verify.finite_markov_tangent_basis(g)[5]
        marginal_score = np.array([-0.7, 0.2, 0.9, -0.3, 0.1])
        marginal_score -= float(g @ marginal_score)
        coefficient = float(
            np.einsum(
                "i,j,ij,i,j->",
                g,
                g,
                q,
                marginal_score,
                marginal_score,
            )
        )
        for parameter in (0.04, -0.03, 0.015):
            perturbed = g * (1.0 + parameter * marginal_score)
            actual = float(np.einsum("i,j,ij->", perturbed, perturbed, q))
            self.assertAlmostEqual(actual, parameter**2 * coefficient, places=14)


class CanonicalHelmertGrowingLayerChecks(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_equal_rate_tail_matches_direct_gap_mass_sum(self):
        for rate in (0.2, 0.7, 1.35, 3.0, 5.0):
            masses = verify._gap_masses(rate, rate, tolerance=1e-17)
            for layer in (0, 1, 2, 5, 10):
                direct = float(np.sum(masses[layer:]))
                exact = verify.equal_rate_gap_tail(rate, layer)
                self.assertLess(abs(direct - exact), 3e-14)

    def test_weighted_helmert_basis_and_layer_moment_bounds(self):
        for rate in (0.2, 0.7, 1.35, 3.0, 5.0):
            for layer in (2, 4, 8, 12, 20):
                gram_error, scaled_envelope, scaled_third_moment = (
                    verify.helmert_layer_diagnostics(rate, layer)
                )
                self.assertLess(gram_error, 2e-12)
                self.assertGreater(scaled_envelope, 0.0)
                self.assertLess(scaled_envelope, 200.0)
                self.assertGreater(scaled_third_moment, 0.0)
                self.assertLess(scaled_third_moment, 1500.0)

    def test_second_order_logarithmic_bracket_has_claimed_signs(self):
        log_n = 200.0
        for rate in (0.35, 1.0, 2.4, 5.0):
            log_log_n = math.log(log_n)
            necessary_inside = math.floor(
                (log_n + 2.0 * log_log_n - 20.0) / (2.0 * rate)
            )
            necessary_outside = math.ceil(
                (log_n + 2.0 * log_log_n + 20.0) / (2.0 * rate)
            )
            sufficient_inside = math.floor(
                (log_n - 2.0 * log_log_n - 20.0) / (2.0 * rate)
            )
            necessary_log_inside = verify.helmert_log_rate_terms(
                rate, log_n, necessary_inside
            )[0]
            necessary_log_outside = verify.helmert_log_rate_terms(
                rate, log_n, necessary_outside
            )[0]
            sufficient_log_inside = verify.helmert_log_rate_terms(
                rate, log_n, sufficient_inside
            )[1]
            self.assertGreater(necessary_log_inside, 5.0)
            self.assertLess(necessary_log_outside, -5.0)
            self.assertLess(sufficient_log_inside, -5.0)

    def test_overlap_vector_has_identity_covariance_and_zero_lag_covariance(self):
        for rate in (0.2, 0.7, 1.35, 3.0, 5.0):
            for layer in (1, 2, 4, 8):
                covariance_error, lag_error, scaled_third_moment = (
                    verify.helmert_overlap_diagnostics(rate, layer)
                )
                self.assertLess(covariance_error, 5e-10)
                self.assertLess(lag_error, 5e-10)
                self.assertGreater(scaled_third_moment, 0.0)
                self.assertLess(scaled_third_moment, 2000.0)

    def test_exact_small_block_third_moments_have_rosenthal_scaling(self):
        for rate in (0.2, 0.7, 1.35, 3.0):
            for layer in (1, 2, 3):
                ratios = [
                    verify.helmert_exact_block_moment_ratio(rate, layer, length)
                    for length in (1, 2, 3, 4)
                ]
                self.assertGreater(min(ratios), 0.0)
                self.assertLess(max(ratios), 40.0)

    def test_cmu_blocking_terms_vanish_inside_sufficient_boundary(self):
        for rate in (0.2, 0.7, 1.35, 3.0, 5.0):
            for log_n in (200.0, 800.0, 3200.0, 12800.0):
                layer = math.floor(
                    (
                        log_n
                        - 2.0 * math.log(log_n)
                        - 10.0
                        - math.sqrt(math.log(log_n))
                    )
                    / (2.0 * rate)
                )
                log_residual, log_gaussian, log_rare = verify.helmert_blocking_log_terms(
                    rate, log_n, layer
                )
                self.assertTrue(
                    all(math.isfinite(value) for value in (log_residual, log_gaussian, log_rare))
                )
            self.assertLess(max(log_residual, log_gaussian, log_rare), -1.0)

    def test_cmu_dimension_factor_exposes_the_open_logarithmic_gap(self):
        log_n = 12_800.0
        for rate in (0.2, 0.7, 1.35, 3.0, 5.0):
            layer = math.floor(log_n / (2.0 * rate))
            _, _, log_rare = verify.helmert_blocking_log_terms(
                rate, log_n, layer
            )
            self.assertGreater(log_rare, 1.0)

    def test_zolotarev_block_terms_close_the_old_cmu_window(self):
        for rate in (0.2, 0.7, 1.35, 3.0, 5.0):
            new_terms = []
            old_rare_terms = []
            for log_n in (200.0, 800.0, 3200.0, 12_800.0):
                layer = math.floor(log_n / (2.0 * rate))
                log_deleted, log_block, log_rare = (
                    verify.helmert_zolotarev_blocking_log_terms(
                        rate, log_n, layer
                    )
                )
                _, old_block, old_rare = verify.helmert_blocking_log_terms(
                    rate, log_n, layer
                )
                log_dimension = math.log((layer + 1) ** 2 - 1)
                self.assertAlmostEqual(log_block, old_block - log_dimension)
                self.assertAlmostEqual(log_rare, old_rare - log_dimension)
                new_terms.append(max(log_deleted, log_block, log_rare))
                old_rare_terms.append(old_rare)
            self.assertLess(new_terms[-1], new_terms[0])
            self.assertLess(new_terms[-1], -4.0)
            self.assertGreater(old_rare_terms[-1], old_rare_terms[0])
            self.assertGreater(old_rare_terms[-1], 1.0)

    def test_critical_window_constant_is_exp_c_over_four(self):
        c = 3.0
        target = c - math.log(4.0)
        for rate in (0.2, 0.7, 1.35, 3.0, 5.0):
            errors = [
                abs(verify.helmert_critical_log_mean(rate, layer, c) - target)
                for layer in (100, 300, 1000, 10000)
            ]
            self.assertLess(errors[-1], errors[0])
            self.assertLess(errors[-1], 0.02)


class SingularExchangeExperimentChecks(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_singular_gap_expansion_is_second_order_and_uniform_on_grid(self):
        for z in (0.12, 0.25, 0.5, 0.78, 0.9):
            diagonal, coefficient = verify.singular_gap_expansion(z, 80)
            for d in (2e-3, 1e-3, 5e-4):
                split = verify.survival_factor_gap_masses(z + d, z - d, 80)
                error = np.max(np.abs(split - diagonal - d**2 * coefficient))
                self.assertLess(error / d**4, 2.0e5)

    def test_singular_score_is_centered_with_positive_information(self):
        informations = []
        for z in np.linspace(0.1, 0.9, 17):
            gap, score, mean_cycle, information = verify.singular_gap_score(
                float(z), tolerance=1e-16
            )
            self.assertLess(abs(float(gap @ score)), 2e-11)
            self.assertAlmostEqual(float(gap.sum()), 1.0, places=12)
            self.assertGreater(mean_cycle, 1.0)
            self.assertGreater(information, 0.0)
            informations.append(information)
        self.assertGreater(min(informations), 1e-5)

    def test_n_quarter_split_is_root_n_in_symmetric_coordinates(self):
        for z in (0.15, 0.5, 0.85):
            for h in (-1.7, -0.4, 0.0, 0.9, 2.1):
                sigma_shift = verify.singular_symmetric_shift(z, h, 100_000_000)
                self.assertAlmostEqual(sigma_shift[0], 0.0, places=14)
                self.assertLess(abs(sigma_shift[1] + h**2), 2e-12)


class SamplingBiasTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_exact_rounded_cycle_mean_matches_gap_tail_sum(self):
        for gamma, kappa, delta in ((0.7, 1.9, 0.4), (1.3, 1.3, 0.2), (3.0, 0.6, 0.1)):
            exact = verify.rounded_cycle_mean(gamma, kappa, delta)
            tail_sum = verify.rounded_cycle_mean_from_tails(gamma, kappa, delta)
            self.assertAlmostEqual(exact, tail_sum, places=12)

    def test_fast_sampling_mean_has_universal_half_interval_term(self):
        gamma, kappa = 0.8, 2.1
        for delta in (0.08, 0.04, 0.02):
            scaled_mean = delta * verify.rounded_cycle_mean(gamma, kappa, delta)
            expansion = (
                1.0 / gamma
                + 1.0 / kappa
                + delta / 2.0
                + gamma * kappa * (gamma + kappa) * delta**4 / 720.0
            )
            self.assertLess(abs(scaled_mean - expansion), 2.0 * delta**6)

   1: \subsection{Pole-order nondegeneracy and the fixed-order serial proof}
   2: \label{subsec:serial-pole-order-proof-main}

   4: \begin{lemma}[Sampled isolated-double-pole nondegeneracy]
   5: \label{lem:sampled-double-pole-nondegeneracy-main}
   6: On \(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), the Palm gap family is analytic in
   7: \((\eta,\delta)\) on a fixed physical one-sided neighbourhood of
   8: \(\delta=0\), obeys the relative bounds in \textup{(SL1)} and \textup{(U1)},
   9: and its one-cycle score coordinates are linearly independent.  Consequently
  10: \textup{(SC16)} holds.
  11: \end{lemma}
  12: 
  13: \begin{proof}
  14: Let \(W=X_1+\cdots+X_n\), where the independent exponential holding times
  15: have rates \(c+\sqrt\delta,c-\sqrt\delta,\theta_3,\ldots,\theta_n\), and put
  16: \[
  17:  B_\eta(s)=\prod_{j=3}^n\frac{\theta_j}{s+\theta_j}.
  18: \]
  19: The empty product is one.  The Laplace transform of the continuous survival
  20: function \(\overline F_{\eta,\delta}(t)=P(W>t)\) is
  21: \[
  22:  H_{\eta,\delta}(s)=\frac1s\left\{1-
  23:  \frac{c^2-\delta}{(s+c)^2-\delta}B_\eta(s)\right\}.
  24: \tag{P1}
  25: \]
  26: At a base point with \(c=\lambda\), direct differentiation gives
  27: \[
  28:  \partial_\delta H_{\eta,0}(s)
  29:  =B_\eta(s)\frac{s+2\lambda}{(s+\lambda)^4},
  30:  \qquad
  31:  \partial_cH_{\eta,0}(s)
  32:  =-\frac{2\lambda B_\eta(s)}{(s+\lambda)^3},
  33: \tag{P2}
  34: \]
  35: and, for \(j\ge3\),
  36: \[
  37:  \partial_{\theta_j}H_{\eta,0}(s)
  38:  =-\frac{\lambda^2}{(s+\lambda)^2}
  39:  \frac{1}{(s+\theta_j)^2}
  40:  \prod_{\substack{\ell=3\\\ell\ne j}}^n
  41:  \frac{\theta_\ell}{s+\theta_\ell}.
  42: \tag{P3}
  43: \]
  44: The displayed expression follows after differentiating
  45: \(\theta_j/(s+\theta_j)\) and cancelling its factor \(s\) against the outer
  46: \(1/s\); all remaining numerator factors are nonzero at the relevant
  47: separated poles.
  48: 
  49: Uniform separation makes \(B_\eta(-\lambda)\ne0\).  Thus
  50: \(\partial_\delta H\) has an exact order-four pole at \(-\lambda\), with
  51: nonzero leading coefficient \(\lambda B_\eta(-\lambda)\), while
  52: \(\partial_cH\) has order three there.  At \(-\theta_j\), the derivative in
  53: \(\theta_j\) has order two, and every other coordinate derivative has at most
  54: order one there.  Inverse Laplace transformation therefore gives the following
  55: distinguishing sampled terms:
  56: \[
  57:  \begin{array}{c|c}
  58:  \text{coordinate}&\text{term not attainable by the remaining coordinates}\ \\
  59:  \hline
  60:  \delta& k^3e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau k}\\
  61:  c& k^2e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau k}\quad\text{after the \(\delta\) coefficient is zero}\\
  62:  \theta_j& k e^{-\theta_j\Delta\tau k}\quad(3\le j\le n).
  63:  \end{array}
  64: \tag{P4}
  65: \]
  66: All leading coefficients in \textup{(P4)} are nonzero.
  67: 
  68: Suppose \(a^\top\dot\ell_{\eta,\delta}=0\) in
  69: \(L^2(g_{\eta,0})\).  Full support gives
  70: \(a^\top\partial g_{\eta,0}(k)=0\) for every \(k\).  Absolute summability
  71: then gives the same identity for the tail derivatives.  Exponential-polynomial
  72: sequences at distinct bases are linearly independent: applying successively
  73: the difference operators \(E-z_j\), or equivalently using their rational
  74: generating functions, separates each base and its highest polynomial degree.
  75: The cubic term at \(e^{-\lambda\Delta\tau}\) first forces
  76: \(a_\delta=0\); the unique linear term at every separated base forces
  77: \(a_{\theta_j}=0\); and the remaining quadratic term at the collision base
  78: forces \(a_c=0\).  The scores are therefore linearly independent.
  79: 
  80: It remains to record the absolute analytic control used for information
  81: continuity.  Formula \textup{(P1)} is rational and analytic in
  82: \((\eta,\delta)\) on a common one-sided neighbourhood whose pole clusters
  83: remain separated by compactness and \(c_0\).  Partial fractions, including
  84: the confluent pole at \(-c\), give for every fixed derivative order
  85: \[
  86:  \sup_{(\eta,\delta)}
  87:  |\partial_{\eta,\delta}^a S_{\eta,\delta}(k)|
  88:  \le C_a(1+k)^{m_a}e^{-\varepsilon\Delta\tau k/2}.
  89: \tag{P5}
  90: \]
  91: First differences give the same absolute bound for \(g\).  The required
  92: relative bounds do not follow from \textup{(P5)}; they are proved independently
  93: in \Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main} by conditioning the complete
  94: holding-time scores on a bin or tail event.  Dominated summation therefore
  95: makes the information continuous.  Pointwise positive definiteness,
  96: continuity, and compactness yield the strictly positive uniform minimum in
  97: \textup{(SC16)}.
  98: \end{proof}
